# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lu_2015_dcds5017a_cyno"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lu_2015_dcds5017a_cyno"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-014-1585-y> (open access, PMC4422865)

The model describes three analytes of an MMAE antibody-drug conjugate (ADC)
at once: the antibody-conjugated MMAE (acMMAE, the conjugate), the total
antibody (Tab, every DAR species including DAR0) and unconjugated MMAE. The
conjugate is resolved into its nine DAR species. Every species shares the
same two-compartment distribution and the same Michaelis-Menten proteolytic
degradation; species with n > 0 MMAE also lose one MMAE at a time by
deconjugation, at a per-MMAE rate constant that falls steeply with DAR
following a Weibull function. Both catabolic pathways feed unconjugated MMAE,
each through its own fraction (Fmp for proteolysis, Fmd for deconjugation).
The MMAE parameters are identified by a separate IV MMAE study in the same
species.

# Population

Lu 2015 fitted 52 cynomolgus monkeys. Thirty-two received DCDS5017A, the
cynomolgus cross-reactive anti-CD79b surrogate ADC (mc-vc-PABC-MMAE, average
DAR about 3.5): single IV doses of 0.3, 1 or 3 mg/kg (4 animals each) and
3 or 5 mg/kg IV every three weeks for four doses (10 animals each). Twenty
received unconjugated MMAE IV at 0.03 or 0.063 mg/kg (10 each). The data
were 447 Tab, 132 acMMAE and 454 unconjugated MMAE concentrations. Body
weights are not reported; the paper takes 2.5 kg as the typical body weight
of a cynomolgus monkey. The model has no covariates, so every simulation
below converts mg/kg doses to nmol at 2.5 kg.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Lu_2015_dcds5017a_cyno")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Nine DAR species, two compartments each, shared Vc / Vp / CLd | -- | Methods 'Model Development'; Fig. 4; Eq. 1-6 |
| Per-species MM proteolysis `Emax * Xn / (Km * Vc + Xn)` | -- | Eq. 1, 3, 5 |
| Sequential deconjugation `n * KADCn * Xn` from DARn to DARn-1 | -- | Eq. 1, 3, 5 |
| MMAE two-compartment, input `Fmp * Amp + Fmd * Amd` | -- | Eq. 7, 8 |
| `Amp = sum n * proteolysis_n`, `Amd = sum n * KADCn * Xn` | -- | Eq. 9, 10 and the text defining Amp and Amd as total MMAE formation |
| `KADCn = K (kappa / lambda) (x / lambda)^(kappa - 1) exp(-(x / lambda)^kappa)`, `x = 8 - n` | -- | Eq. 11 and following text |
| `lvmax` (Emax) | 0.0407 nmol/h | Table I (printed unit 1/h; see Assumptions) |
| `lkm` (Km) | 0.959 nmol/L | Table I |
| `lvc` (Vc) | 0.0996 L | Table I |
| `lq` (CLd) | 0.00197 L/h | Table I |
| `lvp` (Vp) | 0.183 L | Table I |
| `lkdec_wscale` (lambda) | 1.51 | Table I |
| `lkdec_wshape` (kappa) | 1.10 | Table I |
| `kdec_wamp` (K) | 1 1/h, fixed | Text after Eq. 11 |
| `lfm_proteolysis` (Fmp) | 0.783 | Table I |
| `lfm_deconjugation` (Fmd) | 0.0242 | Table I |
| `lcl_mmae` (CLm) | 2.27 L/h | Table I |
| `lvc_mmae` (Vm) | 1.00 L | Table I |
| `lq_mmae` (CLmd) | 23.0 L/h | Table I |
| `lvp_mmae` (Vmp) | 88.4 L | Table I |
| `fdar0` ... `fdar8` | 0.05235, 0.0061, 0.3051, 0, 0.4835, 0, 0.12755, 0, 0.02545 | Methods 'Model Development' (HIC composition of the dosing solution) |
| IIV variances on Emax, Vc, Vp, Fmd, CLm, Vmp | 0.0945, 0.0118, 0.230, 1.78, 0.333, 0.0670 | Table I, 'Inter-individual variability' column |
| `propSd`, `propSd_tab`, `propSd_mmae` | 0.257, 0.194, 0.327 | Table I residual errors |
| MW of DCDS5017A and MMAE | 145239 and 718 g/mol | Methods 'Antibody Drug Conjugates' |

# Simulation helpers

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Lu_2015_dcds5017a_cyno")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui)

bw <- 2.5 # kg, the paper's typical cynomolgus body weight
mw_adc <- 145239
mw_mmae <- 718
adc_nmol <- function(mg_per_kg) mg_per_kg * bw * 1e6 / mw_adc
mmae_nmol <- function(mg_per_kg) mg_per_kg * bw * 1e6 / mw_mmae

# The model declares three endpoints (Cc, Cc_tab, Cc_mmae). Observation rows
# name an ODE state plus dvid = 1, and every endpoint column is returned.
# Each ADC dose is the total antibody amount given to every DAR compartment
# that the dosing solution contains; the model's f() splits it by DAR.
dar_cmts <- paste0("dar", c(0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8), "_central")

adc_events <- function(mg_per_kg, n_dose = 1, ii = 504, obs_times, id_offset = 0, n_id = 1) {
  dose_rows <- expand.grid(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_id),
    time = (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * ii,
    cmt = dar_cmts,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  dose_rows$amt <- adc_nmol(mg_per_kg)
  dose_rows$evid <- 1L
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = id_offset + seq_len(n_id), time = obs_times, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  obs_rows$cmt <- "dar4_central"
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  obs_rows$evid <- 0L
  obs_rows$dvid <- 1L
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    mutate(dose_mgkg = mg_per_kg) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

mmae_events <- function(mg_per_kg, obs_times, id_offset = 0, n_id = 1) {
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_id), time = 0, cmt = "central_mmae",
    amt = mmae_nmol(mg_per_kg), evid = 1L
  )
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = id_offset + seq_len(n_id), time = obs_times, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  obs_rows$cmt <- "central_mmae"
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  obs_rows$evid <- 0L
  obs_rows$dvid <- 1L
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    mutate(dose_mgkg = mg_per_kg) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

# DAR-dependent deconjugation (Figure 8)

Figure 8 of Lu 2015 plots the deconjugation rate of each DAR species, which
is `n * KADCn` (the factor in Eq. 1-6), from 3.52 1/h for DAR8 down to below
0.01 1/h for DAR1. The values below were read from Figure 8 by the
maintainers (DAR8 is the Results text value). The printed Weibull evaluated
at `x = 0` would give DAR8 a rate of exactly zero; the model evaluates the
DAR8 term at `x = 0.01`, which gives 3.51 1/h against the published 3.52 1/h (see Assumptions).

```{r fig8}
rates <- rxSolve(mod_typ, adc_events(1, obs_times = 1), returnType = "data.frame")
fig8 <- tibble(
  DAR = 8:1,
  published = c(3.52, 2.58, 1.15, 0.46, 0.18, 0.065, 0.02, 0.01),
  model = unlist(rates[1, paste0("kdec", 8:1)]) * (8:1)
)
lam <- 1.51
kap <- 1.10
weib <- function(x) (kap / lam) * (x / lam)^(kap - 1) * exp(-(x / lam)^kap)
fig8$printed_x0 <- (8:1) * weib(8 - (8:1))
knitr::kable(
  fig8 |>
    rename(
      "Figure 8 (1/h)" = published,
      "Model n*KADCn (1/h)" = model,
      "Printed Eq. 11, x = 8 - n (1/h)" = printed_x0
    ),
  digits = 4
)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig8$model[1:5] / fig8$published[1:5] - 1) < 0.1))

ggplot(fig8, aes(DAR, model)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = published), shape = 1, size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of conjugated MMAE in ADC", y = "Deconjugation rate (1/h)",
    caption = "Line: model; circles: values read from Figure 8 of Lu 2015."
  )
```

# Unconjugated MMAE after IV MMAE (Figure 7)

The paper reports typical distribution and elimination half-lives of 0.0272 h
and 29.9 h for unconjugated MMAE. These follow from the two-compartment
eigenvalues of the Table I values, and a PKNCA terminal half-life on the
simulated typical profile agrees.

```{r mmae-halflives}
k10 <- 2.27 / 1.00
k12 <- 23.0 / 1.00
k21 <- 23.0 / 88.4
s <- k10 + k12 + k21
alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
hl <- c(distribution = log(2) / alpha, elimination = log(2) / beta)
round(hl, 4)
stopifnot(abs(hl[["distribution"]] / 0.0272 - 1) < 0.01, abs(hl[["elimination"]] / 29.9 - 1) < 0.01)
```

```{r fig7}
mmae_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 2 / 60, 10 / 60, 0.5, 1, 3, 10, 24, 48, 168, 240, 504, seq(0, 60, by = 0.5))))
ev_mmae <- bind_rows(
  mmae_events(0.03, mmae_times, id_offset = 0),
  mmae_events(0.063, mmae_times, id_offset = 1)
)
sim_mmae <- rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_mmae, keep = "dose_mgkg", returnType = "data.frame")

# Representative animals of Figure 7, read by the maintainers (ng/mL)
fig7_obs <- tibble(
  dose_mgkg = rep(c(0.03, 0.063), each = 7),
  time = rep(c(2 / 60, 10 / 60, 1, 3, 10, 24, 48), 2),
  conc = c(28, 1.5, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.09, 50, 3.2, 0.9, 0.85, 0.7, 0.65, 0.4)
)

ggplot(filter(sim_mmae, time > 0, time <= 60), aes(time, Cc_mmae)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig7_obs, aes(y = conc), shape = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg MMAE IV")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Unconjugated MMAE (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 7 of Lu 2015. Line: typical value; circles: one representative animal per dose."
  )
```

```{r mmae-pknca}
mmae_nca_in <- sim_mmae |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc_mmae)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg MMAE")) |>
  select(id, time, Cc_mmae, treatment)
dose_mmae <- ev_mmae |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg MMAE")) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(mmae_nca_in, Cc_mmae ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_mmae, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 504, half.life = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_mmae <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("0.03 mg/kg MMAE", "0.063 mg/kg MMAE"),
  half.life = c(29.9, 29.9)
)
tbl <- ncaComparisonTable(nca_mmae, reference, by = "treatment", params = "half.life", units = c(half.life = "h"))
knitr::kable(tbl)
```

# Single doses of the ADC (Figures 6 and 9)

Typical-value profiles of the three analytes at the three single-dose levels.
Figure 6 shows one representative animal per dose (individual fits), so the
typical curve is not expected to pass through every point; the 3 mg/kg points
read from Figure 6c are overlaid.

```{r fig6}
adc_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 5 / 60, 4, 12, 24, 72, 168, 336, 504, 672, 840, 1008, seq(0, 2000, by = 4))))
ev_adc <- bind_rows(
  adc_events(0.3, obs_times = adc_times, id_offset = 0),
  adc_events(1, obs_times = adc_times, id_offset = 1),
  adc_events(3, obs_times = adc_times, id_offset = 2)
)
sim_adc <- rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_adc, keep = "dose_mgkg", returnType = "data.frame")

long_adc <- sim_adc |>
  filter(time > 0, time <= 1008) |>
  select(dose_mgkg, time, Cc, Cc_tab, Cc_mmae) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cc_tab, Cc_mmae), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = recode(analyte,
    Cc = "acMMAE (nmol/L)", Cc_tab = "Total antibody (ug/mL)", Cc_mmae = "Unconjugated MMAE (ng/mL)"
  ))

fig6c <- tibble(
  analyte = rep(c("acMMAE (nmol/L)", "Total antibody (ug/mL)", "Unconjugated MMAE (ng/mL)"), c(7, 8, 5)),
  time = c(5 / 60, 4, 12, 24, 168, 336, 504, 5 / 60, 4, 12, 24, 72, 168, 336, 504, 4, 12, 24, 72, 168),
  conc = c(2000, 1300, 1000, 700, 90, 15, 0.6, 80, 60, 50, 40, 22, 9, 2, 0.06, 0.045, 0.06, 0.065, 0.07, 0.045),
  dose_mgkg = 3
)

ggplot(long_adc, aes(time, conc, colour = factor(dose_mgkg))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig6c, colour = "black", shape = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1e-3, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration", colour = "Dose (mg/kg)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Lu 2015. Circles: the 3 mg/kg animal of Figure 6c."
  )
```

The release of MMAE into the systemic circulation by each pathway (Figure 9)
is the integral of `Fmp * Amp` and `Fmd * Amd`. Integrating the unweighted
`Amp + Amd` instead must recover every conjugated MMAE in the dose, since
each MMAE leaves the conjugate by exactly one of the two pathways.

```{r fig9}
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
fine <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(0.3, 1, 3)), function(i) {
  adc_events(c(0.3, 1, 3)[i], obs_times = seq(0, 3000, by = 0.25), id_offset = i - 1)
}))
sim_fine <- rxSolve(mod_typ, fine, keep = "dose_mgkg", returnType = "data.frame")
fig9 <- sim_fine |>
  group_by(dose_mgkg) |>
  summarise(
    proteolysis = trap(time, fm_proteolysis * amp),
    deconjugation = trap(time, fm_deconjugation * amd),
    released_total = trap(time, amp + amd),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pct_proteolysis = 100 * proteolysis / (proteolysis + deconjugation),
    conjugated_dose = adc_nmol(dose_mgkg) * sum(c(1, 2, 4, 6, 8) * c(0.0061, 0.3051, 0.4835, 0.12755, 0.02545)),
    fig9_proteolysis = c(9.8, 25.5, 66),
    fig9_deconjugation = c(1.0, 3.0, 3.0)
  )
knitr::kable(
  fig9 |>
    select(dose_mgkg, proteolysis, fig9_proteolysis, deconjugation, fig9_deconjugation, pct_proteolysis, released_total, conjugated_dose) |>
    rename(
      "Dose (mg/kg)" = dose_mgkg,
      "Via proteolysis, model (nmol)" = proteolysis,
      "Via proteolysis, Fig 9 (nmol)" = fig9_proteolysis,
      "Via deconjugation, model (nmol)" = deconjugation,
      "Via deconjugation, Fig 9 (nmol)" = fig9_deconjugation,
      "% via proteolysis" = pct_proteolysis,
      "Amp + Amd released (nmol)" = released_total,
      "Conjugated MMAE dosed (nmol)" = conjugated_dose
    ),
  digits = 2
)
# Mass balance: a solve against its own dose, so a tight bound is correct.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig9$released_total / fig9$conjugated_dose - 1) < 0.005))
```

The Figure 9 amounts are for one animal per dose, with that animal's own
parameters and body weight; the typical 3 mg/kg animal (65 nmol by proteolysis,
2.4 nmol by deconjugation) is close to the Figure 9c animal.

Figure 9d summarises the percentage of systemic MMAE released by proteolysis
across the studied animals after a single ADC dose: median 98%, mean 94%,
range 61-99%. The spread comes mostly from the large between-animal variance
of Fmd (1.78 on the log scale). A stochastic cohort of 200 animals per single
dose level reproduces it.

```{r fig9d}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20150601)
n_per_arm <- 200
ev_mc <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(0.3, 1, 3)), function(i) {
  adc_events(c(0.3, 1, 3)[i], obs_times = seq(0, 2000, by = 2), id_offset = (i - 1) * n_per_arm, n_id = n_per_arm)
}))
sim_mc <- rxSolve(mod, ev_mc, keep = "dose_mgkg", returnType = "data.frame")
pct_mc <- sim_mc |>
  group_by(id, dose_mgkg) |>
  summarise(
    pct = 100 * trap(time, fm_proteolysis * amp) /
      (trap(time, fm_proteolysis * amp) + trap(time, fm_deconjugation * amd)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
summ <- pct_mc |>
  summarise(
    median = median(pct), mean = mean(pct),
    p05 = quantile(pct, 0.05), p95 = quantile(pct, 0.95)
  )
knitr::kable(
  bind_rows(
    summ |> mutate(source = "Model, 600 simulated animals"),
    tibble(median = 98, mean = 94, p05 = NA, p95 = NA, source = "Lu 2015 Figure 9d (range 61-99%)")
  ) |>
    select(source, median, mean, p05, p95) |>
    rename("Source" = source, "Median (%)" = median, "Mean (%)" = mean, "5th pct (%)" = p05, "95th pct (%)" = p95),
  digits = 1
)
stopifnot(abs(summ$median - 98) < 3, abs(summ$mean - 94) < 5)

ggplot(pct_mc, aes(factor(dose_mgkg), pct)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    x = "Single ADC dose (mg/kg)", y = "% of systemic MMAE released by proteolysis",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 9d of Lu 2015 (pooled there across doses)."
  )
```

# Repeated dosing (Supplementary Figure 1)

The supplementary visual predictive checks include the every-three-weeks
regimens. A stochastic cohort of 200 animals per regimen gives the median and
90% interval of the individual-predicted total antibody and unconjugated
MMAE.

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20150602)
vpc_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.25, 6, 24, 72, 168, 336, seq(0, 2016, by = 12), 504 + c(0.25, 6, 24, 72, 168, 336), 1512 + c(0.25, 6, 24, 72, 168, 336, 504))))
ev_md <- bind_rows(
  adc_events(3, n_dose = 4, obs_times = vpc_times, id_offset = 0, n_id = n_per_arm),
  adc_events(5, n_dose = 4, obs_times = vpc_times, id_offset = n_per_arm, n_id = n_per_arm)
)
sim_md <- rxSolve(mod, ev_md, keep = "dose_mgkg", returnType = "data.frame")
md_long <- sim_md |>
  select(id, time, dose_mgkg, Cc_tab, Cc_mmae) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc_tab, Cc_mmae), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(dose_mgkg, analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(conc), lo = quantile(conc, 0.05), hi = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(analyte = recode(analyte, Cc_tab = "Total antibody (ug/mL)", Cc_mmae = "Unconjugated MMAE (ng/mL)"))

ggplot(filter(md_long, time > 0), aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg q3w x 4"), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1e-3, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration",
    caption = "Compare Supplementary Figure 1 of Lu 2015. Between-animal variability only, no residual error."
  )
```

# PKNCA of the single-dose ADC cohort

Lu 2015 reports no non-compartmental parameters for the ADC, so this section
documents the simulated exposure of the three analytes in 100 animals per
single-dose level, sampled at the study's nominal times (pre-dose, 5 min and
4, 12, 24, 72, 168, 336, 504, 672, 840 and 1008 h).

```{r pknca-adc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20150603)
nominal <- c(0, 5 / 60, 4, 12, 24, 72, 168, 336, 504, 672, 840, 1008)
ev_nca <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(0.3, 1, 3)), function(i) {
  adc_events(c(0.3, 1, 3)[i], obs_times = nominal, id_offset = (i - 1) * 100, n_id = 100)
}))
sim_nca <- rxSolve(mod, ev_nca, keep = "dose_mgkg", returnType = "data.frame")
adc_nca_in <- sim_nca |>
  select(id, time, dose_mgkg, Cc, Cc_tab, Cc_mmae) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cc_tab, Cc_mmae), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg"))
# Weeks after a 0.3 mg/kg dose some amounts fall to the ODE solver's absolute
# tolerance and come back as tiny negative numbers; they are zero for NCA.
stopifnot(all(adc_nca_in$conc > -1e-6))
adc_nca_in$conc <- pmax(adc_nca_in$conc, 0)
dose_adc <- ev_nca |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "dar4_central") |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg"), amt = dose_mgkg) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(adc_nca_in, conc ~ time | treatment + analyte + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_adc, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 1008, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_adc <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_adc) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(treatment, analyte, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  mutate(analyte = recode(analyte,
    Cc = "acMMAE (nmol/L)", Cc_tab = "Total antibody (ug/mL)", Cc_mmae = "Unconjugated MMAE (ng/mL)"
  ))
knitr::kable(
  nca_summary |>
    rename("Dose" = treatment, "Analyte" = analyte, "Cmax" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-last (conc*h)" = auclast)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Emax units.** Table I prints Emax in 1/h, but Eq. 1-6 use it as
  `Emax * Xn / (Km * Vc + Xn)` with `Xn` an amount, so Emax must be an amount
  per hour. With Emax = 0.0407 nmol/h, a 2.5 kg monkey and the HIC dose
  composition, the typical profiles track the 3 mg/kg animal of Figure 6c
  (acMMAE about 80 and 15 nmol/L at 168 and 336 h; total antibody about 9 and
  2 ug/mL) and the cumulative MMAE release of Figure 9c (65 versus 66 nmol by
  proteolysis), so the model takes the printed value in nmol/h.
* **DAR8 deconjugation rate.** Eq. 11 with `x = 8 - n` gives exactly zero at
  `x = 0` whenever kappa > 1, which would leave DAR8 with no deconjugation.
  The Results text ('decreased from 3.52 ...') and Figure 8 give 3.52 1/h for
  DAR8, and the other seven Figure 8 points match `n * KADCn` with
  `x = 8 - n`. The DAR8 term is evaluated at `x = 0.01`, the offset that
  gives 3.51 1/h at the Table I lambda and kappa (3.52 published, a gap well inside the rounding of kappa = 1.10, since kappa from 1.095 to 1.105 spans 3.44-3.59 1/h); this offset was
  back-solved by the maintainers and is not printed in the paper.
* **Eq. 9 typographical errors.** As printed, Eq. 9 has `X7c` in the DAR8
  numerator, `X8c` in the DAR7 denominator and an unweighted DAR0 term. The
  text defines Amp as the total MMAE formed by proteolysis, so the model uses
  `sum_n n * Emax * Xn / (Km * Vc + Xn)` for n = 1-8 (DAR0 carries no MMAE),
  matching the per-species terms of Eq. 1-5. The mass-balance check above
  confirms that every conjugated MMAE is released by exactly one pathway.
* **Eq. 2 sign.** Eq. 2 prints `+ (CLd / Vp) * X8p` for the DAR8 peripheral
  compartment; Eq. 4 and 6 give the correct `-` sign, which is used for all
  species.
* **Variability scale.** The Table I 'Inter-individual variability (%CV)'
  column is read as log-scale variances (omega^2), with the parenthetical
  being the precision of the estimate, as in the population-mean column.
  Read as standard deviations the Vc value (0.0118) would be a 1% CV; read as
  variances it is 11%. The Fmd variance of 1.78 reproduces the 61-99% range
  of Figure 9d; as a standard deviation it would push the lower end well
  below 50%.
* **Body weight.** The model uses absolute volumes and clearances. All
  simulations here take the paper's typical 2.5 kg monkey to convert mg/kg
  doses to nmol.
* **Dosing.** A dose is the total antibody amount in nmol given to every
  `darN_central` compartment present in the dosing solution; `f()` applies
  the HIC fractions. DAR3, DAR5 and DAR7 were not detected in the dosing
  solution and have fraction 0.
* **Below-LLOQ handling** (censored likelihood) is an estimation detail and
  has no counterpart in the simulation model.
